questions.question_english: 90. Currency devaluation differs from currency depreciation in that devaluation is:
options_english: Deliberate downward adjustment of currency value by authorities under a fixed exchange regime
Unofficial currency depreciation caused entirely by market forces under a floating exchange regime
Automatic exchange rate appreciation resulting directly from high domestic economic growth rates
A sustained upward rise in domestic currency value relative to foreign benchmark currencies
questions.explanation_english: Currency devaluation is a deliberate downward adjustment of the value of a country's currency by its government or central bank, typically under a fixed exchange rate system. This is in contrast to currency depreciation, which occurs due to market forces in a floating exchange rate system. Devaluation is a policy action, while depreciation is a market-driven phenomenon.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। मुद्रा अवमूल्यन एक जानबूझकर किया गया नीचे की ओर समायोजन है जो सरकार या केंद्रीय बैंक द्वारा किया जाता है, आमतौर पर एक नियंत्रित विनिमय दर प्रणाली के तहत। यह मुद्रा ह्रास से भिन्न है, जो तैरते विनिमय दर प्रणाली में बाजार बलों के कारण होता है। अवमूल्यन एक नीति कार्रवाई है, जबकि ह्रास एक बाजार-प्रेरित घटना है।

68. Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes provided below:
List I: Type of Inflation
P. Demand-Pull Inflation
Q. Cost-Push Inflation
R. Built-In Inflation
S. Hyperinflation
List II: Underlying Cause
I. Increase in production input costs such as wages or raw materials
II. Extremely rapid, out-of-control price increases usually during economic collapse
III. Excess aggregate spending relative to aggregate output capacity
IV. Wage-price spiral where workers demand higher nominal wages to offset cost of living
questions.explanation_english: Demand-Pull Inflation arises when aggregate demand surpasses total aggregate supply capacity. Cost-Push Inflation is driven by increased production costs such as raw materials or wage hikes. Built-In Inflation is linked to wage-price spiral expectations where workers seek higher nominal wages to counteract rising living costs. Hyperinflation is characterized by extremely rapid and uncontrolled price increases that can devastate domestic purchasing power during severe economic downturns.

questions.question_english: 18. Arrange the following Five-Year Plans in the correct chronological order of their implementation period:

Following annual plan gaps, the Fourth Five-Year Plan covered the period from 1969 to 1974. The Fifth Five-Year Plan was operational between 1974 and 1978 before being terminated early. The Janata Party government subsequently launched the Rolling Plan spanning 1978 to 1980.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। भारतीय केंद्रीय योजना अवधियों का कार्यान्वयन क्रम तीसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना से शुरू हुआ, जो 1961 से 1966 तक लागू की गई थी। वार्षिक योजना के अंतराल के बाद, चौथी पंचवर्षीय योजना 1969 से 1974 तक के काल को कवर करती है। पांचवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना 1974 से 1978 के बीच कार्यरत थी, इससे पहले कि इसे जल्दी समाप्त कर दिया गया। इसके बाद जनता पार्टी सरकार ने 1978 से 1980 तक चलने वाली रोलिंग योजना शुरू की।

40. Evaluate the following statements regarding price indices in India:
A. The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) measures price changes at the bulk sale level and does not include the service sector.
B. The Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) is compiled and published by the Labour Bureau.
C. The base year for the Consumer Price Index (CPI-Combined) was recently revised to 2022 by the Office of Economic Adviser.
Which of the statements above are correct?
questions.explanation_english: The Wholesale Price Index measures price movements at the first point of bulk transaction and excludes service sector prices. The Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour compiles the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers. However, the Consumer Price Index Combined (Rural/Urban) is released monthly by the National Statistical Office under MoSPI, and its official base year remains 2012, rather than being revised to 2022 by the Economic Adviser.

questions.question_english: 17. Which noted economist formulated the strategy of heavy industry-led industrialization during India's Second Five-Year Plan?
questions.explanation_english: The strategy of heavy industry-led development implemented during India’s Second Five-Year Plan was formulated by eminent statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis. Known as the Feld’s-Mahalanobis model, this economic framework prioritized state investments in capital goods industries, basic metallurgy, power generation, and heavy industrial machinery. The primary strategy was building domestic capital accumulation capacity to ensure economic self-reliance and accelerate long-term economic growth.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। भारी उद्योग-आधारित विकास की रणनीति, जो भारत की दूसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना के दौरान लागू की गई थी, प्रसिद्ध सांख्यिकीविद् प्रसांत चंद्र महालनोबिस द्वारा तैयार की गई थी। इसे फेल्ड-महालनोबिस मॉडल के रूप में जाना जाता है, यह आर्थिक ढांचा पूंजी वस्तुओं के उद्योगों, बुनियादी धातुकर्म, बिजली उत्पादन और भारी औद्योगिक मशीनरी में राज्य निवेश को प्राथमिकता देता है। प्राथमिक रणनीति आर्थिक आत्मनिर्भरता सुनिश्चित करने और दीर्घकालिक आर्थिक विकास को तेज करने के लिए घरेलू पूंजी संचय क्षमता का निर्माण करना था।

questions.question_english:
71. How is the Primary Deficit in the Union Budget calculated?
By subtracting which item from the Fiscal Deficit?
questions.explanation_english: In fiscal budget accounting, Primary Deficit measures the current financial shortfall in government revenues excluding past accumulated debt obligations. Mathematically, Primary Deficit is calculated by subtracting interest payments on past borrowings from the gross Fiscal Deficit. A zero Primary Deficit indicates that government borrowing is entirely dedicated to paying interest on accumulated past debt rather than funding current operational spending or new investment projects.
